note: Five unglossed citations: sarsari, ṣaaṭ, tase, torati, šahedi. No semantic support for a historical assignment; especially do not identify ṣaaṭ with strength by shape alone.
jak one corresponds to regional yak/ak/ek; initial y/j development and numeral category support the identification.
jakɑːʃ eleven is the one-plus-ten compound, not an independently inherited root accent.
Numeral saat seven, already linked; the citation does not mark its mora.
bat after is plausibly regional baad/bad, but final consonant and source context need checking; no inherited assignment.
pa/patuno temporal after are a grammatical alternation; compare back/postposition pat-, but the precise formation is not established.
sami all could be a regional sam- totality word; do not assign an etymon on meaning alone.
aw and is a regional contact conjunction, likely Pashto; no inherited accent test.
piloo ant and plural pilee share the pil- stem; contracted formation relative to pipīla/pilīla.
pilee is the plural of piloo ant; final ee belongs to the nominal paradigm.
mana apple has no secure match among the supplied Shinaic apple families; leave etymology open.
taqriban approximately is the Arabic-origin regional adverb, a contact item.
terčapera around is a regional adverb/compound; superficial resemblance to turn roots is insufficient.
pare away is a case/adverbial formation of the across/farther-side para family; suffix and direction must be kept separate from noun accent.
azirgala is a place-name citation; no inherited lexical accent assignment.
laganema/laganama baking board appears to contain regional lagan vessel plus another element, but formation and borrowing route remain unresolved.
čambaan-o bark is a verbal citation here; do not compare it to bark of a tree merely because the English gloss matches.
yang battle is regional jang, an Iranian contact item.
hin- versus al- copular stems are grammatically distinct; no single historical headword safely predicts both. Retain all ten cells as unassigned copular evidence.
inʈ͡ʂ bear matches the inherited r̥kṣa set; inčeṛi forms add a feminine/derivational ending, so they do not directly test the bare masculine accent.
daṛi beard matches the regional dāṁṣṭra family; feminine ending and reduced cluster are independent segmental evidence.
šubaaṇ-u beautiful matches older Sauji šobaṇo and the śubhvan family; the printed hyphen separates gender morphology.
bilo became belongs to the bil- perfective, distinguished from baan- imperfective.
ṣači because of is a postposition; no secure lexical reconstruction from these comparanda.
Mixed baan- imperfective and bil- perfective become are assigned separately by stem below.
baan-al-ee become/go has both verbal extension and tense/agreement morphology; root-family link only, not a direct reflex of the Sanskrit finite citation.
baanu becomes is the imperfective becoming stem.
patkeṇo/patkeṇi behind contain back pat- plus extended adjectival/postpositional morphology; suffix accent is unknown.
menǰi between matches madhya and the regional middle postposition; the nasal is retained as an observed segmental difference.
gaan-/gan- big agrees with older Sauji and Palula ghāṇu/ghan-; compare gender and number endings separately.
kašaṇ-i black matches the kr̥ṣṇa family through the known Sauji expanded consonant sequence and feminine ending.
raːt blood belongs to rakta, not the homophonous night set.
haːɖ/haːɖu bone belong together; the final u and bare stem are distinct citation shapes.
kitaab book is the Arabic-origin contact noun.
kitaaba books is the local plural of the contact noun kitaab; useful morphology, not inherited OIA accent.
čeduaṇ-ee borrower has agentive morphology, but the verbal base is not established here.
diːja both plausibly belongs to the two family, but the added j and ending require a full pronominal comparison before assignment.
pu/pi- boy belongs to pōta; ǰitak- boy is a different lexical formation and is left unresolved.
ǰitaka boys is the plural of ǰitak-, not evidence for dāraka simply because both mean boys.
mandili bread matches older Sauji mēṇḍili and the maṇḍa family; diminutive/extended formation remains part of the analysis.
t͡ʃut͡ʃuː breast is the reduplicated cuccu set; expressive origin limits deep accent inference.
si bridge compares to sētu/sīu; contraction removes the original syllable boundary, so mora history cannot be read from unmarked si.
sia bridges is the inflected plural of si bridge.
ataan-/aṭ- bring matches the aṭṭ family only at the lexical-root level; the added imperfective and agreement morphology is retained.
bra/braː brother corresponds to bhrātr̥ with cluster reduction.
brawu brothers is the brother plural; uw morphology prevents treating it as an independent etymon.
daǰaan-u burn contains the intransitive/passive daj- stem comparable to dahyate, not the causative dahayati by default.
xo but/however is the Pashto-type regional conjunction; contact evidence only.
piši cat matches puśśī; the vowel difference and feminine morphology remain visible.
kukuṛ-/kukuṛ-ee chicken is the kukkuṭa set with a plural/oblique ending in the longer form.
laːvu child/small matches older Sauji lau and the laghu property family; semantic nominalization does not create a separate accent history.
paaɣas clean has no demonstrated cognate among the proposed splendid/clean roots; do not assign by gloss alone.
ban close likely belongs to the regional band closure verb/adjective, but context is insufficient for a strict inherited input.
yaan-/yeen-/y- come can be compared to yāti; wol- is a separate perfective stem and remains unassigned.
pačowaan-/pačoaal- cook show causative/tense extensions of pac-; link the lexical family, not the exact inherited finite formation.
peekibo cooked is a pakva-family participial formation with additional morphology; its vowels do not supply accent.
leka counting likely corresponds to the regional lekh reckoning noun, but no input accent should be imputed without the relevant entry.
riŋɡeen-i cry is not segmentally matched to rodati by meaning alone; leave unresolved.
dawudi is a personal name with case morphology; exclude from inherited common-noun inference.
thilo did belongs to the th- do paradigm with a perfective l extension.
muṛ-oo die is a perfective/dead-stem citation; mṛta is the formation comparator, not an unqualified present-root reflex.
muro died is the perfective/dead-stem formation corresponding to mṛta.
rakam different is the regional kind/sort contact word, not an inherited other adjective.
čoor-ee disturb has no secure root assignment in the selected evidence.
thaan-/theen- and thil-/til-/ṭil- are the do paradigm; imperfective, perfective and agreement cells remain separate.
thaanu does is the imperfective do stem with agreement.
kučuroo/kučuri/kučure dog are masculine, feminine or inflected members of kuccura; final oo is a genuine length distinction, not an acute mark.
kučuree dogs is the plural of kučuroo.
kaːɳ ear is already linked to karṇa.
khuwaan-/khaal-/khaa eat represent imperfective, perfective and imperative cells of the khād family.
mačo echo has no secure cognate here; do not confuse it with the fish word.
aɳɖoː egg matches āṇḍa; the long final gender vowel must be distinguished from a short-u adjective ending.
aaš eight is already linked to aṣṭā.
aštiyaš eighteen is the eight-plus-ten compound, with an expanded medial sequence.
yekaaš eleven is the same compound as jakɑːʃ, a transcription/variant pair.
degar evening is the Persian-type time-of-day word, not the inherited vikāla set by meaning alone.
har every is the Iranian regional quantifier.
anʈ͡ʂiː eye matches akṣi through the characteristic affricate outcome and feminine extension; final length alone is not pitch accent.
mox-e face belongs to mukha; -e is case/number morphology, and a secondary mukhya formation remains a possible finer comparison.
baabu father is already linked to the expressive bāppa family.
phanti feather is a pakṣa-family candidate supported by regional phaaṭu-type forms; the nasal and i ending need further phonological explanation, so confidence is provisional.
inčeṛi female bear is assigned to the independently feminine r̥kṣī family rather than treating its ending as part of the masculine citation.
kukuri female chicken is the feminine member of the kukkuṭa paradigm.
kučuri female dog is the feminine member of kuccura, supported by the source's own kučuroo paradigm.
panǰiš fifteen is the inherited five-plus-ten compound; compound accent must be modeled separately.
dešaan dubiša fifty is a vigesimal phrase ten plus two twenties; no single OIA fifty headword is appropriate.
jaŋg fight/conflict is the Iranian jang contact word, same lexical item as yang battle.
aŋguri/anguri finger corresponds to aṅguli with rhotic outcome.
naːkʰ fingernail matches nakha; long aa and retained aspiration are directly observed, accent unmarked.
angure fingers is the plural of anguri.
hangaːru fire corresponds to aṅgāra with initial h and broadened ember-to-fire meaning.
matsiɳ fish contains the matsya stem plus an unexplained final extension; do not assign the rohitamatsya compound because of fish alone.
paanǰ five is already linked to pañca.
xawar flat resembles a regional adjective but lacks a secure reconstruction in the present evidence.
pišu/pišo flour are the piṣṭa nominal set; the grinding verb pēṣayati is related but not the immediate noun formation.
poš-a flower belongs to the regional poś/pōṣ flower set under puṣya; the final a is inflectional.
zaŋgali forest is the regional jangal word with a case/derivational ending; contact versus inherited history is unresolved and no tone is supplied.
dubiša forty is transparently two twenties, a compositional numeral; keep separate from an unmodified twenty reflex.
čoor/čur four are the catvāraḥ set; vowel quantity varies by citation/cell.
čadiš fourteen is already linked to the four-plus-ten compound.
lambaṛi/lumbaṛi fox correspond to the lōmaṭaka regional fox family, with a feminine/extended ending.
biyaal-u frighten plausibly contains the fear root, but causative formation and precise ancestor are not established here.
munɖaːko frog is the maṇḍūka set; modern vowel quality and quantity are separate from inherited accent.
diyon/diyaan/diyo from are grammatical postposition forms; no etymology follows from superficial similarity to a holding root.
asondiyo from us contains the first-person plural pronoun plus the source's diyo postposition; phrase-level grammatical evidence, not a simplex accent reflex.
dito gave corresponds to the datta perfective stem.
pu-yee/poo-yee girl compare to the pōta-family boy/girl paradigm; female and case extensions are retained.
daan-/d- give and dit- given are linked to their separate present and perfective formations below.
daano gives is the present giving stem.
baan- go and g- perfective go require separate vrájati and gata formation links.
baan-al-e go/become is semantically ambiguous between the two source paradigms; no forced historical assignment.
čhaal-u/t͡ʃʰɑːlɛ goat match the chagala set, with sex/number morphology. chāgala is an alternative historical formation, not an interchangeable accent input.
baanu goes is the going imperfective; distinguish the homophonous becoming verb.
xwax good is Pashto-type contact vocabulary; bal is a different citation requiring source-context clarification. Neither is assigned to śubha by gloss.
yarime government is opaque here; a semantic match with rājya is insufficient.
nawaasi granddaughter belongs with regional nawasa/nawasi; borrowing route and deeper formation need investigation, not substitution of pautrī.
nawaasu grandson is the male counterpart of nawaasi; do not equate it with the segmentally different pautra set.
drab grass plausibly reflects darbha with metathesis, an etymological lead needing the full entry; not a reflex of ghāsa by meaning alone.
nil-i green is the nīla adjective with a gender ending; source supplies no accent.
nilbel-ee-n-ee grow has substantial verbal morphology and no secure lexical match; do not assign vardhate solely from the gloss.
haat-/haːtʰ hand matches hasta; haat-o-de is an inflected/postpositional form, not the same citation cell.

la-/le-/li- proximate pronouns form a distinct deictic paradigm. Several cells are explicitly secondary Buddruss citations not confirmed by Knobloch's speakers; retain that distinction and leave deep ancestry open.
se versus t- remote-pronoun stems are suppletive within a paradigm. Link se to sa only; t- requires its own demonstrative formation.
šeš head corresponds to śīrṣa and older Sauji ṣiṣ; source's unmarked spelling is not a tonelessness claim.
bud͡ʒiloː hear plausibly contains a budh/buj knowing/hearing stem, but the prefix and formation are not established; do not force śṛṇoti.
kumaak help is the regional Persian komak contact word.
kukuṛ-/kukuṛi hen are the kukkuṭa bird paradigm; some masculine-shaped citations under hen require the original grammatical cell to be retained.
kukuṛe hens is the plural of the chicken/hen stem.
laadee/lade here are locative formations of the proximal la- demonstrative, not independent lexical roots.
ʂinga horn corresponds to śṛṅga; retained final a prevents a monosyllabic mora comparison.
guṛu horse corresponds to ghōṭa with the regional retroflex-rhotic outcome and masculine ending.
gooš/goš- house belongs to goṣṭha as already linked in this source; case/number alternants differ in root quantity.
keti how many belongs to the kiyatta quantifier set; its final vowel is grammatical, accent unknown.
paanǰbiša/paanǰbisa hundred are five twenties; sawa hundred is a different formation, assigned separately below.
dešaan paanǰbiša hundred and ten is a compositional phrase ten plus five twenties, not an inherited simplex numeral.
ṣubiša hundred and twenty is six twenties; the vigesimal construction must be analyzed as a compound.
buṣaag-u hungry plausibly continues the bubhukṣaka family through the hunger stem plus adjectival ending; cluster simplification and g require further source comparison, so provisional.
ǰaleen-i hurt is a verbal stem with imperfective morphology; resemblance to śūlate is insufficient without a supported affricate correspondence.
miʃa husband belongs to the contracted miš man/husband set, distinct from uncontracted maanuṣ.
ma/mi first-person singular forms belong to the ma pronominal stem, with case variation.
muškani/muxaamšuṇi in front of contain front/face-related material and further morphology; the exact division and borrowing history remain unresolved.
daḍee direction-of is a directional postposition, with no secure lexical ancestor assigned.
ṣaa into is a grammatical item; no lexical cognacy follows from the retrieved English-gloss matches.
hinu/hino is belong to the hin- copula; historical derivation remains open rather than inheriting bhavati accent through a modern translation.
musaaferi/musafari/musaphari journey are Arabic/Persian-origin contact vocabulary; the ph/f variants are transcription/phonological evidence only.
qaziː judge is an Arabic-origin contact noun, here explicitly a secondary Buddruss citation.
kamtili is a place-name citation; no common-noun etymology is assumed.
moraan-/moreen-/moril- kill belong to the causative mārayati family; perfective l and agreement morphology are separated from the root.
morilo killed is the perfective of moraan- kill.
gozan-/gozel- knead form an imperfective/perfective pair, but their base is not a supported mard- reflex.
ḍuṅgo knee may relate to a bent/rounded-body-part term, but it is not a secure kuṭṭha reflex; no forced cognacy.
piyaanil-/piyonaan- know may be a prefixed knowing/recognizing formation; jānāti without the prefix does not establish the history.
hansil-i laugh corresponds to hasati with nasal and perfective extension; the exact finite Sanskrit citation is only a root-family comparator.
paːɬu leaf matches pattra, with the Sauji lateral outcome also seen in three; final u and cluster history distinguish it from pallava.
garazaṛ-ee lender appears related to the regional qarz loan vocabulary, but source segmentation and agentive formation need checking.
zindagi life is the Persian-origin contact noun.
laaw-u/leew-i little show the laghu adjective's gender/umlaut alternation; do not substitute alpa because of the shared meaning.
wosedal/wasedal live preserve a Pashto-type verbal infinitive; contact origin or calqued integration needs primary lexical confirmation.
jiːnuː liver is segmentally unlike yakṛt in these data; leave the lexical replacement unexplained.
čed loan is the base associated with čeduaṇ-ee borrower, but its deeper etymology is unresolved.
agil-u look is not securely linked to lakṣati or dṛkṣati; retain as an unresolved verbal formation.
d͡ʒuj louse belongs to the yūkā set through the widespread ju/jū form; glide quality and final shape remain source observations.
inč male bear is the unextended masculine ṛkṣa comparator.
kukur male chicken is the masculine kukkuṭa stem.
kučuroo male dog is the masculine kuccura form with long final oo.

maanuṣ- man has a retained long first vowel and uncontracted stem, making mānuṣa a plausible formation distinct from miš husband and short-root mánuṣa. Provisional until the exact historical variant is checked; do not infer its accent from length.
bazaar-ee market is the Iranian contact noun with local case morphology.
maṭe/maṭee to me are first-person ma plus the dative ṭe; secondary versus new source attestations remain separate.
ʈ͡ʂir milk is the kṣīra set with affricate outcome; quantity and pitch are not independently resolved by this spelling.
menat-a minute is the modern international time-unit loan with local ending.
rupa-ya/rupai money are the regional rupee noun, a contact currency term; do not assign the red adjective merely because money can be called red in Palula.
yon-e month may continue a moon-related stem, but no secure māsa derivation is supported by these segments.
laalapare morning has more structure than the candidate dawn roots; leave it unresolved without a supported segmentation.
yeey/jeːj mother match āryikā-family contraction and the regional yēy maternal term.
moṛ-u mountain is a separate lexical item from khaṇḍa mountain; the supplied evidence does not establish its root.
naːm name corresponds to nāman; this is source Table2's unaccented phonetic citation, not a marked mora.
keči near is comparable to the regional kacchi near/side set under kaccha; kakṣyā is an alternative formation. The exact ancestor is provisional.
sagardan nervous is the regional Persian sar-gardān type adjective with reduced r; contact history needs confirmation.
nu nine is the contracted nava numeral.
uṛiš nineteen compares to ūnaviṁśati with strong contraction; numeral-series analogy may participate, and the exact phonological steps remain uncertain.
naːs nose corresponds to nasta and the regional nās stem.
na and ne negation have distinct potential formations; assign na to na, leave contracted ne ambiguous between naiva and other negative-copular combinations.
n-eel-i not be is a segmented negative copula; it cannot be treated as a simplex reflex of naiva.
ɖaːgu/ḍag-i old is a masculine/feminine property pair, but no secure relation to jāra or buḍḍha is demonstrated here.
ganu old/big/tall is the same ghan- property family as gaan-o; the age sense does not by itself identify gāḍha.

ganeeroo older is the comparative of gan- big, with the independently visible -eer- suffix. It parallels Palula age comparatives morphologically but is not a direct reflex of gāḍhatara4119. Final long oo is printed without accent.
rate-/rati on is a postpositional paradigm; no exact historical input is established by the accidental lexical-gloss matches.
jak/yak/ek/eki one are members of the one-numeral paradigm; forms differ in initial glide and ending.
dwi other matches the second-to-other development of dutīya; retained w may reflect the two-stem, so the exact derivation is provisional.
taandor-e oven is the regional tandoor contact noun with local case ending.
kačo particles has an underspecified gloss; no reconstruction is defensible without context.
bora-bato Pashto language contains the language/speech word bato of the vārtta family plus an ethnolinguistic modifier; compound, not a bare speech reflex.
paːpi paternal aunt resembles an expressive kinship formation but is not securely established as pitṛṣvasṛ by these segments.
bowṛi paternal uncle is a distinct kin term; do not map it to maternal-uncle mātula by generic uncle meaning.
bowṛiyee ɬeṛi paternal uncle's wife is an analytic kinship phrase, literally uncle's woman/wife. Components can be compared separately; no simplex etymon assigned.
pʰaːnt path corresponds to panthā with the characteristic aspirated outcome and retained nasal-stop cluster.
xalak-a people is regional Pashto/Arabic-origin xalak, integrated with local number morphology.
šair-e poet is an Arabic-origin contact noun with case ending.
talaan-/taleen-/tel- pour constitute a verbal paradigm, but no supported derivation from the retrieved pouring roots exists.
tayar prepare is the regional Arabic-origin ready word used predicatively; not an inherited sanoti reflex.
topos question is the same regional tapos inquiry word grouped under the database's unknown-etymon placeholder. This is lexical comparison only and supplies no reconstructed input.
aya question marker is the Iranian interrogative particle, distinct from the lexical noun topos question.
gooš-ee room is the inflected house word with narrower room meaning, independently attested as house in the same source.
paṛa-yee rope has no secure match to rajju/dāman in this evidence; feminine/case morphology is identifiable but not the root history.
salim is a personal name, not a common-noun sound-law datum.
sau/sau-gaṛi are place-name and demonym material; their deep ancestry is unresolved.
saujibid-ee Sauji language plausibly includes the same speech/language bati stem with compounding reduction; provisional component-level comparison only.
men-aal-oo/men-oo say belong to the regional man/men say set assigned to mantrayate; tense and agreement are separate.
man-ani say/speak/read has the same man- stem; the broad English sense range does not justify a different rásati link.
ʈikut͡ʃ scorpion resembles the regional ṭinčuk/ṭičuk formation under ṭoṅka, but metathesis and the deeper semantic derivation remain provisional.
pašaan- see and deeš-/deš- seen are the independently identifiable present and perfective stems; assign to paśyati and dṛṣṭa separately.
saat seven is the same numeral as the source's digit-glossed citation.
saat-sawa seven hundred is a compositional seven plus hundred expression, not a simple saptá reflex.
satiyaš seventeen is the seven-plus-ten compound with an expanded medial sequence.
dešaan ɬaabiša seventy is ten plus three twenties; retain its vigesimal composition.
ša is a proper-name or insufficiently glossed citation; do not equate it with oath or king without context.
špank-ay shepherd is a Pashto-type shepherd word with local morphology; it is not segmentally a barkarapāla reflex.
šergala is a place name.
paša/pašuwanu/pašuanu show are causatives of the see stem; the optional w is printed as an explicit source alternative.
čaŋ sieve is a different lexical item from paripavana; no secure history is established here.
gošte similar to is a comparative/postpositional item; similarity to the house spelling does not establish cognacy.
beeṇ/bhyeṇ sister corresponds to bhaginī with contraction; source variants preserve different glide/aspiration representations.
beeṇa sisters is the inflected plural of beeṇ.
beeṭ- sit contains the upaviṣṭa-type perfective stem plus further tense/agreement suffixes, distinct from the present viś/bish stem.
ṣo/ʂo six are the ṣaṣ numeral set.
ṣuṛaš sixteen is already linked to ṣoḍaśa.
ɬaabiša sixty is three twenties, not a direct simplex ṣaṣṭi reflex.
gaːɬ skin is not a secure carman reflex; a body/limb term such as gātra could be investigated because of the lateral correspondence, but that is an unverified new proposal.
suaan-/sueen- sleep and sot- slept require svapati versus supta formation comparison; do not map the entire paradigm to one finite headword.
law-ee small is the plural/oblique laghu adjective form.
ǰandraaw snake corresponds to the extended jantu family and Palula jhandurā, with final aw and nominal extension retained.
sum soil clearly matches Palula/Shina sum lexically, but their database súmahānt link is explicitly very doubtful. Record the cross-language lexical set without propagating that old-accent input.
ade/aḍe some are quantifier forms whose exact historical formation remains open.
aḍi-bi some/also combines the quantifier with an additive particle; do not treat it as one inherited root.
bati/bata speech belong to the vārtta tidings/speech family and older Sauji bātya.
qaʃuq spoon is the Turkic-origin regional spoon word, a secondary Buddruss citation here.
taːri star belongs to tārā with a feminine ending; modern stress unmarked.
šaank-ee stick compares to šaŋko wood and the śākhya/śākhā branch family; nasal and immediate derivative remain uncertain, so provisional.
baːʈ stone corresponds to varta and the regional baṭ stem.
baːʈa stones is the plural of baːʈ, with final a retained.
kamaqal stupid is the Persian/Arabic kam-aql compound, a contact adjective.
suːri/suri sun belongs to sūra with final i; the source gives quantity variants without accent analysis.
sure suns is the plural of suri.
terčapera surrounding repeats the around adverb; its internal history remains unresolved.
meez table is the Persian contact noun; meez-aan is an inflected cell, not a different etymon.
meeza tables is the local plural of borrowed meez.
daːnda teeth is the plural of daːnd tooth, corresponding to danta.
deš/dɛʃ/daš ten belong to daśa; source variants differ in vowel representation.
Mixed demonstratives se/t- remote and la proximal must be separated; se alone is assigned to sa, while the other stems remain unresolved.
Remote plural se/t- forms belong to one suppletive demonstrative paradigm, but not one unqualified old headword; se alone receives the sa link.
ganeere elders/leaders is the plural/substantivized age comparative of gan- big; independent -eer- morphology parallels ganeeroo older.
bi and giri then are separate discourse particles; no common historical input is warranted.
giri then/again resembles a turn/again adverb but lacks a demonstrated route from phirati; leave unresolved.
le-/lin- proximal plural pronouns are the la- paradigm's number/case alternants; preserve secondary-source labels and unknown ancestry.
Remote plural se/t- pronouns have suppletive stem formation; only se is assigned to sa.
muṣaaṛi thief plausibly derives from a steal root muṣ- with an agentive suffix, a useful etymological lead; exact formation and accent are unresolved.
troyiš thirteen is the three-plus-ten compound and should be compared to the teen series, not the simple numeral three.
dešaan biš thirty is ten plus twenty, not a direct triṁśat reflex.
aštiyašaan biš thirty-eight is eighteen plus twenty; preserve the phrase's composition.
panǰišaan biš thirty-five is fifteen plus twenty.
čadišaan biš thirty-four is fourteen plus twenty.
uṛišaan biš thirty-nine is nineteen plus twenty.
yakaašaan biš thirty-one is eleven plus twenty.
satiyaašaan biš thirty-seven is seventeen plus twenty.
ṣuṛešaan biš thirty-six is sixteen plus twenty.
troyišaan biš thirty-three is thirteen plus twenty.
baašaan biš thirty-two is twelve plus twenty.
la-/le-/li- this forms belong to the proximal demonstrative paradigm; no supported derivation from ayam or ana is established.
le/lena/lini/leni this-plural are proximal plural/case forms, several cited secondarily from Buddruss.
ɬaa three corresponds to trayaḥ with the diagnostic Sauji tr-to-lateral outcome.
anguṭo thumb corresponds to aṅguṣṭha and older Sauji aṅguṭho; aspiration loss and ending are explicit differences.
gan tie matches granthayati-family knot/tying stems; exact verbal formation remains distinct from the Sanskrit finite citation.
vaxti/waxta time are inflections of the Arabic-origin regional waqt word.
ṭe/ṭee and diya to are separate postpositional forms; no simplex lexical ancestor assigned.
di towards is a grammatical directional item with unresolved deeper history.
ṭee to/towards/at is the same dative postposition found after pronouns, not an independent content-word etymon.
si together is a comitative item; its short form alone does not establish a derivation from sārtha.
si together with is the same comitative as si together; ancestry unresolved.
ǰib/d͡ʒib tongue corresponds to jihvā with the regional b outcome.
ǰiba tongues is the plural of ǰib.
daːnd/daːndu tooth correspond to danta; bare and u-ending forms are distinct cells/shapes.
torsan is a place-name citation.
keeṇi towards is a directional form whose relation to the -keṇ- postposition series merits study; no accent input assigned.
musaːpʰar traveler/journey is the Arabic/Persian-origin musāfir contact word; semantic nominal use does not make it inherited OIA vocabulary.
ǰul-e tree compares to the jhalla forest/tree family; narrowed versus broad vegetation senses are plausible, but exact vowel history remains uncertain.
baaš twelve is already linked to dvādaśa.
